question: Should OpenClaw accept this restart-specific durable SQLite audit table with redacted source/session/preflight metadata and a fixed 512-row retention cap before broader audit-ledger work?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and tested, but the permanent local metadata boundary, retention policy, and restart-path write placement are product/security ownership choices rather than mechanical code defects.

options.title: Accept the restart audit contract
options.body: Merge after explicitly accepting the table, fields, redaction policy, retention cap, and post-transition write placement as the intended operator-forensics boundary.

options.title: Narrow persisted metadata first
options.body: Require a smaller field set or stricter redaction/retention policy before adding durable restart audit rows.

options.title: Defer to broader audit ledger
options.body: Pause this PR if restart audit persistence should wait for a unified audit-ledger design instead of adding a restart-specific producer now.

recommendation.title: Accept the restart audit contract
recommendation.body: Merge after explicitly accepting the table, fields, redaction policy, retention cap, and post-transition write placement as the intended operator-forensics boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest restart/gateway ownership trail and is the best available owner for the product boundary decision.
